newsitem.title: FINLAND: VALMET SAYS BELOIT PATENT CASE OFF TRACK.
newsitem.headline: VALMET SAYS BELOIT PATENT CASE OFF TRACK.

text.p: Finnish paper machine maker Valmet Oy said on Monday a U.S. rival Beloit was trying to throw a patent dispute court case off track by linking it to an offset trade agreement between Finland and the United States.

"It should be a completely normal routine court case about a patent dispute, we have had a number of these for the past 25 years," Valmet senior vice president and general counsel Harri Luoto told Reuters by telephone.

He was commenting on media reports that a Wisconsin senator had asked U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno to investigate if airplane maker McDonnell Douglas Corp had used the offset trade system to help foreign firms compete with U.S. companies.
The patent dispute is connected with an order won by Valmet in June to deliver a paper machine to Willamette Industries of the United States, to come on stream in April 1998.

According to Luoto, Beloit claims McDonnell Douglas, referring to its own offset trade obligation linked to Finland's purchase in the early 1990s of U.S. Hornet fighter aircraft, had pressured Willamette to award the order to Valmet.
Beloit is part of U.S. mining equipment and paper and pulp machine group Harnischfeger Industries Inc based in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.
"Now Beloit can state in court that Reno is investigating the matter, further obscuring the real issue," Luoto said. "This has nothing to do with the patent case at hand.
"It is complete nonsense anyway because the Finnish offset trade committee has not even cleared the paper machine sale as an offset trade item," he said.

The idea of the offset trade arrangement is that the jet fighter seller, McDonnell Douglas, is obliged to arrange export opportunities for Finnish companies so that the value of these so called offset deals will match the about 12 billion markka price paid by Finland for the Hornet aircraft.
The Finnish offset trade committee is authorised to approve or reject proposed offset deals.
Luoto said the offset system was intended for the benefit of smaller Finnish companies whose products are unknown in the U.S., not for well established firms like Valmet.
He said Valmet may seek to have all its contracts permanently excluded from the offset trade list to avoid further conflicts like the current one with Beloit.
